correctness.rationale: The domain \(\Omega(n)\le2\) is exhausted by primes, prime squares, and squarefree semiprimes. The formulas \(S(p)=p\), \(S(p^2)=2p\), and \(S(pq)=q\) are proved directly from factorial valuations. Small boundary cases give exactly 2, 3, 6, and 15; a monotone exact factorial ratio proves every semiprime with larger prime factor at least 7 satisfies the inequality. A separate finite checker found no contradiction through 200000.

value.rationale: The focal theorem leaves the exceptional set structurally unspecified. Classifying the complete \(\Omega(n)\le2\) layer is a natural multiplicative-complexity boundary: it identifies every low-complexity failure and proves that any additional exception must have at least three prime factors counted with multiplicity. The contribution is an infinite exact classification with a cutoff-free proof, not a finite table extension.
